title: Follow-up examination of entrapment syndromes and nerve injuries via ultrasound and electrophysiology
summary: Injuries to nerves in the arms and/or legs are common and lead to relevant impairments for the affected patient. Such nerves can be damaged by pressure at anatomical bottlenecks, e.g. in carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) or sulnar neuropathy of the elbow (UNE). However, the nerve can also be crushed, pulled or severed as a result of an injury. High-resolution nerve ultrasound is a new examination method that promises significant diagnostic improvements. Over a study period of around 3 years, 80 patients with surgically treated carpal tunnel syndrome, 80 patients with conservatively treated carpal tunnel syndrome, 50 patients with UNE- surgery, 50 patients with conservatively treated UNE and 80 patients with (traumatic) nerve injuries will be examined (before surgery or at diagnosis, after 2 weeks, after 4 weeks, after 6 months). Standardized questionnaires/scores for the existence of a disease of several to all nerves (so-called polyneuropathy) (Neuropathy Symptom Score (NSS), Neuropathy Deficit Score (NDS), Overall Neuropathy Limitations Scale (ONLS)) as well as standardized questionnaires on CTS (Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ)) and UNE (Ulnar Neuropathy of the Elbow Questionnaire (UNEQ)) will be collected. Current measurements (electroneurography and electromyography) are used to measure the affected nerve as well as the dependent muscle and the unaffected opposite side. Ultrasound will be used to examine both the affected nerve and the unaffected opposite side. The planned project will investigate the diagnostic strength/safety of nerve ultrasound for the diagnosis of the aforementioned bottleneck syndromes and nerve damage. In particular, it will also be investigated whether concomitant polyneuropathy makes diagnosis by ultrasound more difficult. In the further course of the planned project, the standardized course of nerve damage using ultrasound will also be described for the first time.

interventions.name: Patients with symptoms typical of carpal tunnel syndrome who receive conservative treatment
Patients with symptoms typical of carpal tunnel syndrome who receive surgical treatment
Patients with symptoms typical of ulnar neuropathy of the elbow who receive conservative treatment
Patients with symptoms typical of ulnar neuropathy of the elbow who receive surgical treatment
Patients with a clinically suspected peripheral nerve lesion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical signs of carpal tunnel syndrome, ulnar neuropathy of the elbow or another peripheral nerve lesion
Exclusion criteria:
Neuromuscular disease of another cause (e.g. myasthenia gravis, ALS, etc.), active underlying malignant disease, current or previous use of neurotoxic medication (e.g. chemotherapeutic agents, nitrofurantoin, etc.). For CTS/UNE patients: previous surgery due to CTS/UNE.
